metadata.description: Scenario-based study companion for the CCA-F certification — covers agentic architecture, Claude API patterns, tool design, MCP integration, prompt engineering, and operational best practices.

question.title: Agentic Loop Design
question.scenario: A development team is building an agent that uses Claude to autonomously complete multi-step coding tasks. The agent needs to decide when to call tools, when to ask for clarification, and when to return a final result. The architect is choosing between a single-pass prompt and an agentic loop.
question.question-text: Which architectural pattern allows an AI agent to iteratively use tools and refine its approach across multiple turns before delivering a final answer?

choices.choice: Single-shot prompt with all instructions included upfront
Agentic loop with tool calls, observation, and reasoning steps
Batch processing pipeline with no intermediate feedback
Static template expansion with variable substitution

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: An agentic loop lets the model call tools, observe results, and decide next steps iteratively.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: An agentic loop is a pattern where the AI model repeatedly cycles through reasoning, tool use, and observation. At each step, Claude decides whether to call a tool, interpret a result, or deliver a final answer. This is more powerful than single-shot prompting because it allows the agent to adapt its strategy based on intermediate results, handle errors, and break complex tasks into manageable steps.

ul.li: Agentic loops typically follow the pattern: Think → Act (tool call) → Observe (tool result) → Repeat or Return.
Claude's tool-use capability enables structured tool calls with JSON schemas, letting the orchestrator execute actions and feed results back.
Key design considerations include setting maximum iteration limits, implementing graceful degradation, and defining clear stop conditions to prevent infinite loops.

question.title: Claude API Message Structure
question.scenario: A backend engineer is integrating Claude into a customer support application. They need to send a conversation history to the Claude API and receive a response. They are reviewing the API documentation to understand how to structure the request.
question.question-text: In the Claude Messages API, which role is used to provide instructions that guide Claude's behavior across the entire conversation?

choices.choice: The "user" role in the messages array
The "system" parameter at the top level of the request
The "admin" role in the messages array
The "config" parameter in the model settings

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: The system prompt is a top-level parameter, not a message role.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: In the Claude Messages API, the system prompt is specified as a top-level "system" parameter in the request body, separate from the messages array. It provides persistent instructions that guide Claude's behavior throughout the conversation. The messages array contains alternating "user" and "assistant" roles representing the conversation turns. There is no "admin" or "config" role in the API.

ul.li: The system prompt is processed before the conversation messages and has strong influence on Claude's behavior, tone, and constraints.
Best practices include putting role definitions, output format requirements, and safety guidelines in the system prompt.
The system parameter accepts either a string or an array of content blocks, allowing mixed text and cache-control directives for prompt caching.

question.title: Prompt Engineering for Reliable Output
question.scenario: A data team wants Claude to extract structured information from unstructured customer feedback emails. They need the output in a consistent JSON format every time, but initial attempts produce inconsistent formatting and occasionally include extra commentary outside the JSON.
question.question-text: Which prompt engineering technique is MOST effective at ensuring Claude returns only valid JSON without extra commentary?

choices.choice: Ask Claude to "try its best" to output JSON
Provide a few-shot example of the exact JSON schema and instruct Claude to output only the JSON object with no additional text
Increase the temperature parameter to encourage creativity in formatting
Send multiple requests and pick the one that looks most like JSON

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Showing Claude the exact output format you expect is more reliable than vague instructions.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Providing few-shot examples of the desired JSON schema, combined with explicit instructions to output only the JSON object with no surrounding text, is the most reliable technique. This gives Claude a concrete template to follow and a clear constraint on what to include. Vague instructions ("try your best") lead to inconsistent results, higher temperature increases randomness, and retry-based approaches are wasteful and unreliable.

ul.li: For maximum reliability, combine few-shot examples with prefilling the assistant response (starting with an opening brace) so Claude continues the JSON directly.
Using lower temperature values (e.g., 0.0) further reduces variability in structured output tasks.
Claude also supports tool-use responses with JSON schemas, which can enforce structured output at the API level rather than relying solely on prompt engineering.
